metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with a deployable web entry point is present: a Struts 1 Action class (src/com/acme/loan/LoanAction.java) bound to the HTTP path /loan by WEB-INF/struts-config.xml, packaged and deployed as a single WAR per README.md. One service unit only (not a monorepo), with a deployable entry point (not a library), and application code present (not infrastructure-only or deployment-config). Classified as application.
metadata.archetype_justification: The service owns persistent state and mutates it: LoanAction.saveApplication opens a JDBC connection to Oracle and performs an INSERT into the applications table on submit, attributing the row to the authenticated officer. There are no queue consumers (not event-processor), no downstream service calls at all (not orchestrator), and write operations exist alongside the read/quote path (not data-gateway or stateless-utility). Classified as stateful-crud, which is also the conservative default rubric for the four archetype-calibrated questions.
metadata.surface_flags_rationale: has_persistent_data_store=true — LoanAction.java loads the Oracle JDBC driver and opens a DriverManager connection to jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB. has_at_rest_data_surface=true — implied by the persistent data store. has_deployed_workload=false — no Dockerfile, no IaC defining compute, and no deployment manifests; README.md documents a manual WAR upload performed outside this repository. has_api_surface=true — WEB-INF/struts-config.xml declares the HTTP action mapping /loan. has_multi_instance_deployment=false — single WebLogic host on Solaris per README.md. has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false — no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Pulumi, or SAM anywhere in the tree.
notes: Analysis is read-only; no repository source or configuration was modified.
additionalPlanContext supplied no repo_type, service_archetype, context, priority, tags, or preferences; all were inferred from in-repo evidence and recommendations use neutral technology language.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Overall score 1.19 falls in the Not Ready band (≡ Not Ready tier) while the unified severity counts (11 High, 20 Medium, 1 Low) match the '2-11 High → Remediation Required' rule. The divergence is a boundary effect: High findings require internal_score==1 on one of the 14 core questions, and 5 of the 37 questions resolved to Not Evaluated under surface gating (INF-Q9, SEC-Q1, OPS-Q5, OPS-Q7, OPS-Q9), three of which (OPS-Q5, OPS-Q9, SEC-Q1) would otherwise have been core-question candidates. Scoring and surface gating were re-reviewed and are correct as recorded, so the divergence is documented rather than corrected. Both lenses agree on direction: this repository needs broad remediation before any modernization pathway can be executed safely; read the tier as 'Remediation Required, at the Not Ready end of the band'.

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: A production database password is in version control and in the shipped WAR, is present in git history, and is duplicated in a second location. There is no rotation, no access audit, and the credential cannot be changed without a rebuild and redeploy.
top_gaps.impact: Deployment-blocking security exposure: a live production credential is in git history and in the shipped WAR. Must be rotated before any migration work starts.

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: There are no module boundaries, no layering between controller / domain / persistence, and shared mutable request state. Nothing can be scaled, deployed, or tested independently.
top_gaps.impact: Gates every pathway — no module boundaries means nothing can be extracted, scaled, or deployed independently, and the thread-safety defects are a direct consequence.

top_gaps.title: Managed Databases
top_gaps.gap: All persistence runs on a self-managed, end-of-life commercial engine with no managed backups, failover, or patching. The host is referenced by a hardcoded hostname, so any migration requires a code change.
top_gaps.impact: Self-managed EOL Oracle on a single on-premises host is the largest operational and data-loss risk in the system, and blocks the compute migration.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: Build and deploy are entirely manual, with no automated test, no artifact versioning (jars are committed with no version manifest), and no rollback path. There is nowhere to insert quality or security gates.
top_gaps.impact: Manual WAR upload with no tests or rollback makes every change high-risk and leaves nowhere to add quality or security gates.

top_gaps.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
top_gaps.gap: Every infrastructure category this service depends on — compute, networking, the Oracle data store, and monitoring — is provisioned manually (ClickOps / data-center build). Environments are not reproducible and disaster recovery cannot be automated.
top_gaps.impact: With zero IaC, no environment is reproducible; this is the prerequisite workstream for containers, managed databases, and DevOps.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: No managed compute of any kind. README.md documents the runtime as Oracle WebLogic Server 10.3 on Solaris 10 with Java 5, deployed as a WAR file. No `aws_ecs_*`, `aws_eks_*`, `aws_lambda_*`, or `aws_instance` resources exist because the repository contains no IaC at all, and no Dockerfile or Kubernetes manifest was found anywhere in the tree.
findings.gap: 100% of compute is a self-managed on-premises application server appliance. There is no elastic scaling, no managed patching, and the README notes the Solaris host is the last one in the data center — a single-host dependency.
findings.recommendation: Replatform the WAR onto managed compute. Shortest path: containerize the application (Tomcat/Jetty-compatible build or a supported WebLogic container image) and run it on ECS Fargate or EKS; re-architecture to Lambda is only viable after decomposition (see Move to Cloud Native). Treat the Java 5/Struts 1 upgrade as a prerequisite because supported base images do not ship Java 5.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The database is a self-managed Oracle 11g instance. `LoanAction.java` connects directly via `jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB` using `DriverManager.getConnection`, pointing at a named on-premises host. No `aws_rds_*`, `aws_dynamodb_*`, or other managed database resource exists in the repository.
findings.gap: All persistence runs on a self-managed, end-of-life commercial engine with no managed backups, failover, or patching. The host is referenced by a hardcoded hostname, so any migration requires a code change.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a managed service: Amazon RDS for Oracle as a lift-and-shift step to remove the operational burden immediately, or Aurora PostgreSQL as the cost-optimized target (see Move to Managed Databases). Externalize the JDBC URL to configuration before migrating so cutover does not require recompiling the WAR.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service is used. The quote-then-submit flow is hardcoded in `LoanAction.execute()`, which branches on a form field (`if ("submit".equals(lf.getAction()))`) and dispatches via Struts forwards declared in `WEB-INF/struts-config.xml`. No `aws_sfn_*` resources, Temporal SDK, or workflow definitions were found.
findings.gap: The multi-step loan pricing and submission process is implicit in controller code and XML forwards, with no retry, compensation, or state visibility. A failure in `saveApplication` leaves no durable record of the attempt.
findings.recommendation: For the identified `stateful-crud` archetype the rubric expects a dedicated orchestration service for business-critical multi-step operations. Model the quote → submit → confirm sequence in AWS Step Functions (or keep it in-process but extract it into an explicit, testable workflow service) so retries and failure states are observable.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists, managed or self-managed. The repository contains no `aws_sqs_*`/`aws_sns_*`/`aws_kinesis_*`/`aws_msk_*` resources and no messaging client imports; `LoanAction.java` imports only `java.sql` and Struts/servlet APIs. Loan submission writes synchronously to Oracle inside the HTTP request thread.
findings.gap: Scored against the `stateful-crud` archetype rubric: a state change of record (a submitted loan application) is committed with no event emitted, so no downstream consumer — audit, notification, underwriting — can react without polling the database. There is no self-managed broker to decommission, which keeps this at Needs Work rather than Not Ready.
findings.recommendation: When the application is replatformed, publish a domain event (e.g., `LoanApplicationSubmitted`) to Amazon EventBridge or SQS at commit time so notification and downstream processing decouple from the request path. Do not introduce a self-managed broker.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network configuration exists in the repository — no VPC, subnet, or security group definitions, no Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, and no service-mesh rules. The documented deployment is a WebLogic server on a Solaris host in a corporate data center (README.md), with the database addressed by a flat hostname (`dbprod01`).
findings.gap: The repository owns no network surface and provides no segmentation, isolation, or least-privilege controls. There is no evidence of tiering between the web application and the database.
findings.recommendation: Define the target network topology as IaC during migration: private subnets for the application and database tiers, least-privilege security groups permitting only the application tier to reach port 1521, and VPC endpoints for AWS service access. Nothing should be reachable from 0.0.0.0/0 except a managed entry point.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: No managed entry point is defined. Requests reach the application through the Struts action servlet mapping `/loan` declared in `WEB-INF/struts-config.xml`; README.md describes direct WAR deployment to the WebLogic admin console with no load balancer, API Gateway, or CDN in front of it.
findings.gap: There is no throttling, request validation, centralized authentication, or health-check-driven routing. The application server is itself the edge.
findings.recommendation: Place an Application Load Balancer in front of the replatformed workload for health checks and TLS termination, and an API Gateway (REST or HTTP API) in front of any endpoints that are extracted as services, enabling throttling and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration exists. There are no `aws_autoscaling_*` or `aws_appautoscaling_*` resources, no Kubernetes HPA, and no scaling settings of any kind; capacity is a single statically provisioned Solaris host per README.md.
findings.gap: Capacity is fixed and cannot respond to load. This compounds the thread-safety defect the README reports under load ('ActionForms hold mutable shared state; thread-safety bugs under load'), since the only scaling lever is vertical.
findings.recommendation: After containerization, configure ECS service auto-scaling or EKS HPA with target tracking on request count and CPU, and set min/max capacity explicitly. Scale the data tier separately (RDS read replicas or Aurora Auto Scaling) once the database is managed.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration was found. The repository defines no `backup_retention_period`, no `aws_backup_plan`, no snapshot lifecycle, and no documented restore procedure; the only persistence is the self-managed Oracle 11g instance referenced in `LoanAction.java`.
findings.gap: Loan applications — the system of record for submitted business transactions — have no in-repo evidence of automated backup, point-in-time recovery, or tested restore. Recovery capability is unverifiable.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to RDS/Aurora and enable automated backups with an explicit retention period and point-in-time recovery, add the data store to an AWS Backup plan, and document plus rehearse the restore procedure.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No infrastructure as code exists. A full-tree scan found no `.tf`/`.tfvars` files, no CloudFormation or SAM templates, no CDK app, no Helm chart, no Kustomize overlay, and no Ansible playbook. The only configuration artifacts are the Struts action mapping (`WEB-INF/struts-config.xml`) and the application source.
findings.gap: Every infrastructure category this service depends on — compute, networking, the Oracle data store, and monitoring — is provisioned manually (ClickOps / data-center build). Environments are not reproducible and disaster recovery cannot be automated.
findings.recommendation: Establish IaC as the first modernization workstream: define compute, networking, the managed database, secrets, and CloudWatch alarms in Terraform or CDK, and make the pipeline the only path to change. This is a prerequisite for every other pathway in this report.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No CI/CD automation exists. There is no `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `buildspec.yml`, or `appspec.yml` in the repository. README.md states the build is Apache Ant with dependency jars committed into `/lib` and that deployment is a 'Manual WAR upload via WebLogic admin console'.
findings.gap: Build and deploy are entirely manual, with no automated test, no artifact versioning (jars are committed with no version manifest), and no rollback path. There is nowhere to insert quality or security gates.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a pipeline (CodePipeline/CodeBuild or GitHub Actions) that builds the artifact from a declared dependency manifest, runs tests, and deploys through IaC. Replace the committed `/lib` jars with Maven or Gradle dependency declarations so the build is reproducible and scannable.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: Java on a compound-legacy stack. README.md records Java 5, Apache Struts 1.3 (end of life since 2013), WebLogic 10.3, and an Ant build with jars committed to `/lib` and no version manifest. `LoanAction.java` extends `org.apache.struts.action.Action` and uses the raw JDBC `DriverManager` API; no AWS SDK is present at any version.
findings.gap: All three axes are regressed simultaneously — language runtime (Java 5), framework (Struts 1.3, EOL and unpatched), and SDK/build tooling (no dependency manifest, no AWS SDK). Java itself is a first-class cloud-native language, so the gap is version and framework debt rather than language choice.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a supported Java LTS (17 or 21) and migrate the web layer off Struts 1 to Spring Boot 3.x, introducing Maven/Gradle dependency management. This upgrade is the gating prerequisite for containerization and for any AWS SDK v2 integration.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: A single tightly-coupled deployable unit. The application is one WAR with one Struts action module (`com.acme.loan`); `LoanAction.execute()` mixes HTTP request handling, the amortization business calculation, and direct JDBC persistence in the same class, with connection credentials as class constants. README.md additionally reports that 'ActionForms hold mutable shared state; thread-safety bugs under load', confirming pervasive shared mutable state rather than module boundaries.
findings.gap: There are no module boundaries, no layering between controller / domain / persistence, and shared mutable request state. Nothing can be scaled, deployed, or tested independently.
findings.recommendation: Decompose incrementally rather than rewriting — see the Decomposition Strategy section. The immediate step is internal layering: extract the amortization calculation into a pure domain service and the INSERT into a repository class, which makes both unit-testable and creates the seam for later extraction.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication
findings.description: All communication is synchronous and in-process. `LoanAction.execute()` performs the calculation and, on submit, calls `saveApplication` inline, which opens a JDBC connection and commits within the HTTP request. No message publishing, queue consumer, or event handler pattern exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Against the `stateful-crud` archetype rubric this is Score 1: no async path exists for any flow, so the request thread holds a database connection for the full submission and no state change is propagated to other systems. Every future integration would have to be a synchronous call added into the same request path.
findings.recommendation: Introduce async propagation for state changes as part of replatforming: emit a domain event on successful submission (EventBridge/SQS) and move notification or downstream underwriting work out of the request path. Synchronous handling remains correct for the quote calculation, which is a fast pure computation.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Every operation is synchronous regardless of duration. There is no background job framework, no job-status endpoint, and no queue worker in the repository; `saveApplication` performs connection setup (`Class.forName`, `DriverManager.getConnection`) and the INSERT inside the user's request.
findings.gap: Scored on the `stateful-crud` rubric: all operations are synchronous with no async job infrastructure available. Database or network slowness on the Oracle host translates directly into held HTTP threads, which is the documented failure mode under load.
findings.recommendation: Where submission-time work grows beyond the request budget (document generation, credit-bureau calls, batch export), move it to an SQS-backed worker or Step Functions execution and return a job identifier the client can poll. A connection pool is the minimum immediate fix for the per-request connection setup.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: No versioning of any kind. The single action path is `/loan` in `WEB-INF/struts-config.xml`, with forwards to `/quote.jsp` and `/confirm.jsp`. There are no `/v1/` path segments, no version headers, no OpenAPI specification, and no changelog file in the repository.
findings.gap: Any change to the form contract or the forward targets is a breaking change delivered directly to all users, with no compatibility window.
findings.recommendation: When the HTTP surface is rebuilt during migration, adopt a single explicit versioning convention — URL path versioning (`/v1/loans`) is the simplest — publish an OpenAPI specification, and define a deprecation policy before the first consumer integrates.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All endpoints are hardcoded. The database endpoint is a compile-time constant in `LoanAction.java` (`private static final String DB_URL = "jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB"`), duplicated — per the in-code comment — in a `db.properties` file inside the WAR. No service registry, service mesh, or discovery client is present.
findings.gap: Relocating or failing over the database requires editing source and rebuilding the WAR, and the duplicated connection details can drift between the two locations. There is no dynamic resolution of any dependency.
findings.recommendation: Externalize all endpoints to configuration resolved at runtime — SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager for the database endpoint and credentials — and use AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect for service-to-service resolution once services are extracted. Remove the duplicated `db.properties` copy.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: No managed object storage is used and no parsing pipeline exists. The repository contains no `aws_s3_bucket` definition and no document-handling code; the only non-database artifacts are files shipped inside the WAR, including the `db.properties` file referenced in the `LoanAction.java` comment, which lives on the application server's local filesystem.
findings.gap: The application's only storage surfaces are a relational database and the local filesystem of a single Solaris host. A loan origination workflow typically accumulates applicant documents, and there is no managed, durable, searchable location for them.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Amazon S3 as the durable store for any document or generated-artifact content, with server-side encryption and versioning, and add Amazon Textract for extraction if applicant documents are introduced. Eliminate reliance on application-server local disk as part of containerization, since container filesystems are ephemeral.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Data access is inline in the controller with no abstraction. `LoanAction.saveApplication` loads the driver with `Class.forName("oracle.jdbc.driver.OracleDriver")`, opens its own `Connection` via `DriverManager`, builds SQL by string concatenation, and closes the connection in the same method. There is no DAO, repository, ORM, or connection pool anywhere in the repository.
findings.gap: There is no single point of data contract: every action class would repeat connection management and SQL construction. The pattern also produces the SQL injection defect noted in-code ('String-built SQL - applicant name not parameterized') and leaks connections on exception, since `close()` is not in a finally block.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a repository/DAO layer with a managed connection pool (HikariCP) as the sole data access path, and use bound parameters (`PreparedStatement` placeholders) rather than string concatenation. This is both the security fix for the injection defect and the seam required for later schema separation.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: The engine is past end of life and is not pinned in any deployment configuration. README.md states 'Database: Oracle 11g (EOL)'. There is no IaC and therefore no `engine_version` parameter anywhere; the version is implicit in the manually built on-premises instance, and the only in-code reference is the legacy `oracle.jdbc.driver.OracleDriver` class name.
findings.gap: Running an EOL engine means no security patches for the data tier that holds loan applications, and the absence of version pinning means the deployed version cannot be asserted or reproduced from the repository.
findings.recommendation: Treat the engine upgrade as urgent and couple it with the managed-database migration: move to a supported RDS for Oracle version or Aurora PostgreSQL, pin `engine_version` explicitly in IaC, and document the version-update and rollback procedure.

findings.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
findings.description: Business logic is in the application layer, not the database. The amortization calculation is Java code in `LoanAction.execute()`, and no `.sql` files, `CREATE PROCEDURE`, `CREATE TRIGGER`, `CREATE FUNCTION`, or Flyway/Liquibase migrations exist in the repository. The residual coupling is raw string-built SQL executed against Oracle and a hardcoded reference to the proprietary `oracle.jdbc.driver.OracleDriver` class.
findings.gap: No stored-procedure extraction work is required, which materially lowers engine-migration effort. The remaining gap is minor: SQL is hand-built in the controller and the Oracle driver class is hardcoded, so the statement text and driver reference must be reviewed on any engine change.
findings.recommendation: Keep business logic in the application layer. Move SQL behind a repository abstraction with bound parameters and load the JDBC driver from configuration rather than a literal class name, so an engine change is a configuration change. No schema-logic extraction project is needed.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest is configured or referenced. The repository contains no `aws_kms_key` resource, no `kms_key_id` parameter, and no encryption settings of any kind; the Oracle 11g data store reached via `jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB` is provisioned outside this repository with no in-repo evidence of TDE or volume encryption.
findings.gap: Loan applications containing applicant names and financial terms are persisted with no demonstrable encryption at rest and no key management, rotation policy, or key access audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with a customer-managed KMS key on the target managed database (and on any S3 bucket introduced), define a rotation policy, and restrict key usage via key policy. Capture these settings in IaC so the control is enforced rather than configured by hand.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: Authentication is delegated to the container with no token-based mechanism. `LoanAction.execute` calls `request.getRemoteUser()` and stores the result as the originating officer, which implies WebLogic container-managed authentication (declarative form or BASIC auth). There is no OAuth2 or JWT validation, no authorizer, no Cognito integration, and `WEB-INF/struts-config.xml` declares no security constraint on the `/loan` action.
findings.gap: The identity used for the audit field comes from static credential-based container authentication rather than a verifiable per-request token, and authorization is not enforced at the action level — any authenticated user can submit for any applicant.
findings.recommendation: Move to token-based per-request authentication (OIDC/JWT validated at an API Gateway authorizer or by Spring Security) and enforce authorization explicitly on the submit operation. Preserve the officer attribution by deriving it from the verified token subject rather than `getRemoteUser()`.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider integration exists. The repository contains no `aws_cognito_*` resource, no OIDC or SAML configuration, and no federation metadata; identity is resolved entirely by the WebLogic container realm behind `request.getRemoteUser()`.
findings.gap: Loan officer identities are managed in the application server's own realm with no SSO, no central lifecycle (joiner/mover/leaver), and no shared access policy with the rest of the estate.
findings.recommendation: Federate authentication to the organization's IdP — Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML/OIDC federation, or direct integration with the existing enterprise IdP — and retire the container realm so officer accounts are centrally provisioned and deprovisioned.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: Plaintext database credentials are committed to source control. `LoanAction.java` declares `private static final String DB_USER = "loan_app"` and `private static final String DB_PASS = "loanApp2010"` as class constants, with an in-code comment stating the connection details are 'also duplicated in db.properties'. README.md confirms 'Connection details in a properties file inside the WAR'. No Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, or Vault usage exists.
findings.gap: A production database password is in version control and in the shipped WAR, is present in git history, and is duplicated in a second location. There is no rotation, no access audit, and the credential cannot be changed without a rebuild and redeploy.
findings.recommendation: Treat this as an active incident: rotate the `loan_app` database password immediately, then move the credential to AWS Secrets Manager (or RDS/Aurora IAM database authentication) retrieved at runtime, with automatic rotation enabled. Remove the constants and the `db.properties` copy, and purge the credential from git history.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching or vulnerability scanning evidence exists. The repository has no SSM agent configuration, no `aws_ssm_patch_baseline`, no hardened base image reference, no Inspector or Snyk configuration, and no `.github/dependabot.yml` or `renovate.json`. README.md documents Java 5, Struts 1.3 ('end of life since 2013; no security patches'), WebLogic 10.3, and Solaris 10 — all unsupported — with dependency jars committed to `/lib` and no version manifest.
findings.gap: Nothing in the stack receives security patches, and because dependencies are committed binaries with no manifest, the vulnerable component inventory cannot even be enumerated. Struts 1.x in particular has publicly known unpatched vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Replace the committed `/lib` jars with a declared Maven/Gradle manifest so dependencies can be inventoried and scanned, enable Dependabot or Renovate on the repository, adopt managed/hardened base images with Amazon Inspector enabled on the resulting container images, and prioritize the Struts and Java runtime upgrades.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: There is no pipeline and therefore no security validation stage. No SAST tool (SonarQube, Semgrep, CodeGuru), no dependency scanning configuration, and no container image scanning were found; the repository has no CI configuration files at all. Static review found a SQL injection defect — `saveApplication` concatenates `lf.getApplicantName()` directly into the INSERT statement — that an automated SAST gate would have surfaced.
findings.gap: No automated security validation exists anywhere in the delivery path, and the injection defect plus the committed credential demonstrate the practical consequence.
findings.recommendation: When the CI/CD pipeline is created (INF-Q11), include a dependency scan and a SAST stage from day one with a gate that blocks on critical findings, plus ECR image scanning once containerized. Add the existing SQL injection and hardcoded-credential findings as the first items to remediate.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation exists. There are no OpenTelemetry or X-Ray dependencies (and no dependency manifest at all — README.md states jars are committed to `/lib`), no trace context propagation, and no `traceparent`/`X-Amzn-Trace-Id` handling in `LoanAction.java`.
findings.gap: Request flow through the application and into the Oracle database is unobservable. Diagnosing the thread-safety and load issues the README reports relies on log inspection and reproduction in the shared UAT environment.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry (or the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry) during the framework upgrade, exporting to X-Ray or an existing APM backend, and propagate trace context across the HTTP entry point and JDBC calls so database latency is attributable per request.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No monitoring or SLO artifacts exist. The repository contains no SLO definition file, no CloudWatch alarm definitions (there is no IaC), and no latency or error-rate thresholds in any configuration. Evaluated because the service exposes an HTTP surface (`/loan` in `WEB-INF/struts-config.xml`) and owns persistent data.
findings.gap: There is no stated availability or latency target for the loan quoting and submission journey, so degradation cannot be detected or prioritized objectively.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for the two critical journeys (quote latency, submission success rate), implement them as CloudWatch alarms or a service-level dashboard in IaC, and track an error budget. Note that SLO tooling frequently lives in an external monitoring platform; this score reflects in-repo evidence only.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are published. `LoanAction.java` emits no metric calls of any kind — no `putMetricData`, no metrics client, no counters — and no dashboard definitions exist in the repository. Business events such as quotes generated and applications submitted are written only as database rows.
findings.gap: Operational and business outcomes (submission volume, quote-to-submit conversion, failure rate by officer) are invisible without ad hoc SQL against the production database.
findings.recommendation: Publish custom CloudWatch metrics (or OpenTelemetry metrics) for quote and submission counts, failures, and latency at the point of the business event, and build a dashboard alongside the infrastructure metrics.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured. There are no CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, and no paging integration in the repository — consistent with the complete absence of IaC and monitoring configuration.
findings.gap: Failures are detected by users rather than by monitoring. The documented load-related thread-safety defects would surface as user-reported incidents.
findings.recommendation: Define alarms on error rate and p99 latency in IaC and enable CloudWatch anomaly detection on those metrics once a baseline exists, routed to an on-call destination (SNS → paging tool).

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: There are no automated tests of any kind. The repository contains a single source file (`src/com/acme/loan/LoanAction.java`) and no test directory, test framework dependency, or test configuration. README.md states explicitly: 'No unit tests; "testing" is a shared UAT environment'.
findings.gap: There is no automated regression safety net. This is the single largest risk multiplier for every pathway in this report — decomposition, framework upgrade, and database migration all depend on being able to verify behaviour is preserved, and today that verification is manual in a shared environment.
findings.recommendation: Before refactoring, add characterization tests around the amortization calculation (a pure function, trivially testable once extracted) and integration tests for the submission path using Testcontainers against the target engine. Run them in the new CI pipeline as a merge gate.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: No observability ownership artifacts exist. There is no CODEOWNERS file, no per-service dashboard or alarm definition, and no team attribution anywhere in the repository. The only ownership signal is a source comment naming the original author ('Author: D. Whitfield, 2010. Last change 2017').
findings.gap: No team owns monitoring for this service, and no dashboards or alarms exist to own. Operational knowledge is concentrated in code comments and the README's 'Known Issues' list.
findings.recommendation: Assign explicit service ownership (CODEOWNERS plus an owner tag on the deployed resources), create a per-service dashboard with named alarm owners, and attribute the SLOs from OPS-Q2 to that team.

evaluations.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
evaluations.reason: This system has no deployed workload requiring HA evaluation. INF-Q9 does not apply. Surface flag has_deployed_workload=false — the repository contains no Dockerfile, no IaC defining compute, and no deployment manifests; README.md describes a manual WAR upload performed outside this repository. (The single-host Solaris deployment is nonetheless a genuine availability risk and is captured under INF-Q1.)

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: Audit logging (CloudTrail) is an AWS account-level service provisioned once per account or organization - not per-application. This repo contains no AWS-provisioning IaC at all (has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false), so there is no account-level scope to evaluate. CloudTrail evaluation belongs in the foundation/account-level infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Deployment Strategy
evaluations.reason: No deployed workload found in this repo - deployment strategy cannot be assessed from source code alone (has_deployed_workload=false). README.md documents a manual WAR upload via the WebLogic admin console, which is performed outside the repository; the resulting lack of staged rollout is captured under INF-Q11 (CI/CD Automation).

evaluations.title: Incident Response Automation
evaluations.reason: No deployed workload found in this repo - there is no running system defined here to automate incident response for (has_deployed_workload=false). Runbooks and self-healing automation would live in a separate operations or deployment-config repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: This repo provisions no AWS resources (has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false), so there are no resources to tag. Tagging governance belongs in the repo that owns the AWS infrastructure.

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary APP-Q2 = 1 (< 3) AND supporting INF-Q1 = 1, APP-Q3 = 1, APP-Q4 = 1 (all < 3).

triggering_questions.note: Primary — tightly-coupled single WAR with shared mutable state
Supporting — all compute on self-managed WebLogic/Solaris

detail.current_state: Single Struts 1.3 WAR on WebLogic 10.3/Solaris 10. LoanAction.execute() combines HTTP handling, the amortization calculation, and JDBC persistence; ActionForms carry mutable shared state (README 'Known Issues').
detail.compute_gaps: No managed compute, no containers, no auto-scaling (INF-Q1 = 1, INF-Q7 = 1).
detail.communication_gaps: Fully synchronous request-path persistence with no event emission and no async job path (APP-Q3 = 1, APP-Q4 = 1, INF-Q4 = 2).
detail.recommended_approach: Conditional / Adaptive — upgrade the runtime and containerize first, then extract selectively. See the Decomposition Strategy section.
immediate_actions: Extract the amortization calculation into a pure, unit-testable domain service
Extract JDBC access into a repository class with a connection pool and bound parameters
Upgrade Java and replace Struts 1 before attempting extraction

pathways.name: Move to Containers
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary INF-Q1 = 1 (< 3) AND no container definitions found in discovery (no Dockerfile, docker-compose, or Kubernetes manifest). Guard passes: compute is a VM-based WebLogic/Solaris deployment, not Lambda/Fargate/ECS.

triggering_questions.note: Primary — WAR on WebLogic 10.3 / Solaris 10, zero managed compute

detail.current_compute: Manually built Solaris 10 host running WebLogic Server 10.3 with Java 5; WAR deployed by hand via the admin console. README notes this is the last Solaris host in the data center.
detail.container_readiness: Low. Blockers: Java 5 (no supported base image), Struts 1.3 EOL, dependency jars committed to /lib with no manifest, database credentials compiled into the WAR and duplicated in db.properties, and reliance on application-server local disk.
detail.recommended_platform: ECS on Fargate for the lowest operational overhead; EKS if the organization already standardizes on Kubernetes. ECR for images with image scanning enabled.
detail.migration_approach: Refactor-then-containerize. A straight lift-and-containerize is not viable because no supported container base image provides Java 5 or a patched Struts 1; the runtime/framework upgrade (APP-Q1) is a hard prerequisite.
immediate_actions: Replace committed /lib jars with a Maven or Gradle dependency manifest
Upgrade to Java 17+ and migrate off Struts 1
Externalize configuration and secrets so the image carries no credentials
Author the Dockerfile and ECS task definition in IaC

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary DATA-Q4 < 3 AND commercial DB engines detected. DATA-Q4 = 3, so the primary condition is not met.

triggering_questions.note: Primary not met — no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL constructs found; business logic is in Java
Supporting condition IS present — commercial Oracle 11g engine detected in the INF-Q2 finding

pathways.not_triggered_reason: The commercial-engine supporting condition is satisfied (Oracle 11g), but the primary trigger is not: DATA-Q4 scored 3 because no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL constructs exist in the repository — the amortization logic lives in Java. The absence of database-resident logic is what keeps this pathway untriggered, and it also means an engine change would be comparatively low-effort if license cost reduction becomes a driver. Engine modernization is covered under Move to Managed Databases, which recommends Aurora PostgreSQL as the cost-optimized target.

pathways.name: Move to Managed Databases
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary INF-Q2 = 1 (< 3) — self-managed Oracle 11g. Supporting DATA-Q3 = 1 (engine past EOL, no version pinning) strengthens the case.

triggering_questions.note: Primary — self-managed Oracle 11g on an on-premises host
Supporting — Oracle 11g is past EOL and no engine version is pinned in any deployment config

detail.current_topology: Single self-managed Oracle 11g instance reached at jdbc:oracle:thin:@dbprod01:1521:LOANDB, provisioned manually outside the repository. No managed backups, failover, or patching evidence (INF-Q8 = 1, SEC-Q2 = 1).
detail.engine_eol: Oracle 11g is past end of life (README.md). No engine_version pinning exists because there is no IaC.
detail.data_access_patterns: Scattered and unabstracted — DriverManager connections and string-built SQL inline in the controller (DATA-Q2 = 1), with no connection pool. Endpoint and credentials are compile-time constants, so cutover currently requires a rebuild.
detail.recommended_targets: Two-step: RDS for Oracle on a supported version to remove operational burden with minimal code change, then Aurora PostgreSQL as the cost-optimized target. The absence of stored procedures (DATA-Q4 = 3) makes the second step unusually tractable.
immediate_actions: Externalize the JDBC URL and credentials out of LoanAction.java before any migration
Introduce a repository layer and connection pool so the data access path is single-point
Run AWS SCT to size the Oracle → Aurora PostgreSQL conversion
Enable automated backups, PITR, Multi-AZ, and a customer-managed KMS key on the target

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary INF-Q4 = 2 (< 3) is met, but the contextual guard blocks the pathway: no evidence of data processing workloads exists in the repository.

triggering_questions.note: Primary threshold met but guard-blocked — no messaging or streaming infrastructure exists, and none is required by the current surface

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard: evidence of data processing workloads must exist. Discovery found no streaming infrastructure, no ETL or pipeline definitions, no Glue jobs or Airflow DAGs, no data lake configuration, and no analytics queries — the repository contains one Struts action, one action-mapping XML, and a README. This is a transactional loan-entry application with no analytics responsibility, so recommending managed analytics infrastructure would not address a real gap.

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Primary INF-Q10 = 1 (< 3) AND INF-Q11 = 1 (< 3) — zero IaC and zero CI/CD. Supporting OPS-Q6 = 1 (no tests) strengthens the case; OPS-Q5 was Not Evaluated under surface gating and does not count toward triggering.

triggering_questions.note: Primary — no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Ansible anywhere in the repository
Primary — Ant build with committed jars; manual WAR upload via the WebLogic admin console
Supporting — no automated tests; README states testing is a shared UAT environment

detail.iac_coverage: 0%. Every infrastructure category the service depends on — compute, networking, the Oracle data store, secrets, monitoring — is provisioned by hand.
detail.cicd_state: None. No .github/workflows, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or appspec.yml. Apache Ant build with dependency jars committed to /lib and no version manifest; deployment is a manual WAR upload.
detail.deployment_strategy_gap: OPS-Q5 was Not Evaluated (no deployed workload defined in this repo), but the manual admin-console upload documented in the README means there is no staged rollout, traffic shifting, or rollback path.
detail.testing_gaps: No unit or integration tests exist (OPS-Q6 = 1). This is the primary risk multiplier for every other pathway.
detail.recommended_toolchain: Git-based pipeline with CodePipeline/CodeBuild (or GitHub Actions), Terraform or AWS CDK for infrastructure, and CodeDeploy for blue/green release once the workload is containerized.
immediate_actions: Introduce a dependency manifest (Maven/Gradle) so the build is reproducible and scannable
Create a build-test pipeline and add characterization tests for the amortization logic as the first gate
Define the target environment as IaC and make the pipeline the only path to change
Add dependency scanning and SAST stages to the pipeline from day one (SEC-Q7)

pathways.name: Move to AI
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: Contextual guard not satisfied — the pathway requires AI/agent/LLM intent evidenced in the repository, and the primary trigger was therefore not evaluated.
pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation). A case-insensitive scan of README.md, WEB-INF/struts-config.xml, and src/com/acme/loan/LoanAction.java found none of the AI signal terms, and there is no dependency manifest to scan. The guard blocks evaluation of the primary trigger.

decomposition_strategy.recommendation_rationale: APP-Q2 = 1 (no module boundaries, pervasive shared mutable state) normally argues against incremental extraction, but two factors change the calculus here: the codebase is very small (one action class, ~57 lines of Java) and the business logic that matters — the amortization formula — is already in the application layer with no stored procedures to untangle (DATA-Q4 = 3). The binding constraints are the unsupported runtime (Java 5 / Struts 1.3) and the total absence of tests (OPS-Q6 = 1), not architectural size. The correct sequence is therefore: add characterization tests, upgrade the runtime and framework, containerize as a single unit, and only then extract services if independent scaling or team autonomy becomes a real driver. Full microservice decomposition is not justified by the current scale.

approaches.assessment: Viable and partly necessary regardless of the end state. Introduce layering (controller → domain service → repository), remove shared mutable ActionForm state, and give the data access path a single owner. 2-6 months of internal refactoring at this codebase size, mostly consumed by the Java/Struts upgrade.

Normally the default for a monolith, but at ~57 lines of business code there is little to strangle. Keep it in reserve: if the loan domain grows, route new capability through a new service behind an Anti-corruption Layer rather than back into the Struts WAR.

RECOMMENDED. Upgrade runtime and framework, containerize the application as-is, migrate the database to a managed service, then extract only what demonstrably needs independent scaling. Delivers the operational wins (managed compute, managed data, CI/CD) without an architectural rewrite.

RECOMMENDED AGAINST. With no automated tests and no written specification beyond the README, feature parity cannot be verified and regression risk is severe. The amortization behaviour and APR cap added in 2017 exist only in code.

patterns.when: On any new service that must read loan data, to avoid inheriting the current table structure and string-built SQL conventions.
Immediately — it is the concrete form of the controller/domain/repository split that makes the amortization logic testable and the JDBC layer replaceable.
Only if loan submission later spans multiple services (e.g., pricing, credit check, document generation) and loses its single database transaction.
If regulatory audit requires a durable history of quote and submission events; today only final-state rows are written.

effort_factors.signal: High effort — no boundaries; one class holds HTTP, domain, and persistence concerns (APP-Q2 = 1)
High effort signal in pattern but low in volume — unabstracted inline JDBC (DATA-Q2 = 1) across a single small module
Low effort — none found; business logic is already in Java (DATA-Q4 = 3)
High effort — entirely synchronous, no async primitives to build on (APP-Q3 = 1)
High effort — no pipeline exists to extend (INF-Q11 = 1)
High effort — zero automated tests; the dominant risk factor (OPS-Q6 = 1)

decomposition_strategy.calibrated_estimate: Low to Medium for the recommended Conditional/Adaptive path, dominated by the Java 5 → Java 17+ and Struts 1 → Spring Boot 3 upgrade and by building the missing test safety net — not by decomposition itself.
